final_message:
Adapter: rank 2, on model.layers.15.mlp.down_proj only. ||dW||_F = 0.46, compared with ||W||_F = 16.4. The edited model was never run, as the rules require, so its effect on pass rate is a prediction.

What the unedited model gets wrong (76 of my own MBPP-style tasks with hidden tests, greedy, thinking off):
- Baseline pass rate is about 0.41 / 0.29 / 0.56 on three task sets.
- Main cause: after a correct function it keeps going with "\n\n\n# Test..." and writes its own asserts inside the code block. Those asserts are often wrong, or loop until the token limit (unterminated strings, SyntaxError).
- Second cause: it renames the function (second_largest_distinct, split_list_into_chunks, argmax_index...), so the hidden tests hit a NameError.
- If I strip the code back to just the definitions, the pass rate rises to 0.59 / 0.39 / 0.69.
- Adding an instruction to the prompt ("just the function in a python block, exact name from the test, no tests or explanation") raises the pass rate to 0.69 / 0.54. So these are behaviour problems, not missing ability.

Where the decision happens (from analysis of the unedited model):
- token_stats on the same reply with and without the instruction shows two decision points.
  - Function end: after the last code token, the plain model gives "\n" (which leads to closing the block) only about 4% and prefers "\n\n\n" or "\n\n".
  - Function name: the name tokens.
- The instruction's effect on the residual stream at these points appears around layers 12–16 and is very consistent across tasks (cosine ≈ 0.87 at resid.16).
- Copying just the instructed resid.16 into the plain run at a single position is enough. At the function end, "\n" goes from 4% to 60%. At the name, the bad "_dist" continuation goes from 26% to 4%, and the correct "(nums" becomes the top token.

The edit (closed-form, no training):
- Steering directions B: the average instructed-minus-plain difference at resid.16, taken (a) at function-end positions (24 tasks) and (b) at `d
